title: Copilot Studio: block maker-provided credentials for tool authentication
summary: The briefing is largely supported by Microsoft Learn and matches the roadmap record. However, the Threat detection path skips selecting an environment or environment group before Set up, so the exact administrative instructions need correcting.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Control maker credential options lets administrators restrict how makers authenticate agent tools.
claims.quote: Controlling the use of maker-provided credentials is a governance feature in Microsoft Copilot Studio that allows administrators to determine how makers can authenticate tools they add to agents.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: A tool configured with maker credentials uses the maker's permissions for agent users and can expose information or actions those users cannot otherwise access.
claims.quote: When someone uses the agent, the agent uses the maker's credentials, not the end user's credentials, to authenticate with connected services.

claims.claim: Administrators can permit end-user credentials, maker-provided credentials, or both.
claims.quote: You choose whether makers can select to use their own credentials for authenticating tool connections, to use the end-user's credentials, or to have access to both.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The restrictive control is admin-opt-in: both End-user and Maker-provided credentials are enabled by default.
claims.quote: By default, both End-user and Maker-provided credentials are enabled.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; controls[0].note; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Restricting maker credentials immediately removes makers' ability to select their own credentials.
claims.quote: When configured as instructed, the feature immediately turns off the maker's ability to select their credentials for authenticating tools within the environment or environment group.

claims.where: What's changing; controls[0].note; Governance controls table; Governance controls
claims.claim: Enforcing end-user credentials changes all tools for all agents in the affected environments to require end-user credentials at runtime.
claims.quote: All tools for all agents in the impacted environments instantly change to require end-user credentials at runtime.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: Before rollout; rationale: impact
claims.claim: New conversations with affected agents prompt users to sign in to the connected service.
claims.quote: Enforcing the use of end-user credentials prompts the end user to sign in (to the relevant service or connector) when needed. ... the agent might use that existing authentication session.
claims.fix: Qualify the sign-in descriptions with 'if needed'; the same Learn page says existing authorized sessions can be reused, so not every new conversation necessarily presents a fresh sign-in prompt.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Why it matters
claims.claim: Enforcing end-user credentials confines connected-service actions to the end user's own permissions.
claims.quote: The action runs under the end-user's identity. If the user lacks permission for something, the agent is unable to do it on their behalf - by design.

claims.claim: No stored maker credentials are used at runtime when end-user credentials are enforced.
claims.quote: No stored maker credentials are used at run time, aligning the agent's behavior with the end user's actual permissions.

claims.claim: With maker credentials prevented, each tool call requires authentication with a live user's sign-in.
claims.quote: When maker-provided credentials are prevented from being used, agents require real-time user interaction because each tool call must be authenticated with a live user sign-in.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: Before rollout; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Agents triggered by scheduled events fail due to missing credentials when maker credentials are prevented.
claims.quote: agents triggered by scheduled or autonomous events, or that attempt to run in the background, fail due to missing credentials.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: Before rollout; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Agents triggered by autonomous events fail due to missing credentials when maker credentials are prevented.
claims.quote: agents triggered by scheduled or autonomous events, or that attempt to run in the background, fail due to missing credentials.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Agents attempting to run in the background fail due to missing credentials when maker credentials are prevented.
claims.quote: agents triggered by scheduled or autonomous events, or that attempt to run in the background, fail due to missing credentials.

claims.claim: All agent triggers must involve an active user when maker credentials are prevented.
claims.quote: All agent triggers must involve an active user.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Makers who previously configured tools with their own credentials might be prompted to change them before publishing.
claims.quote: If the maker previously had a tool configured with their credentials, they might be prompted to change it before publishing the agent.

claims.claim: The control covers connectors, built-in actions and embedded Power Automate flows equally.
claims.quote: The control over the authentication type covers connectors, built-in actions, and embedded Power Automate flows equally.

claims.claim: A Power Automate flow used as an agent tool requires each user to sign in for the connections that flow uses.
claims.quote: A Power Automate flow as a tool in the agent also requires each user to sign in for any connections that flow uses.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope; controls[0].scope; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The credential policy applies per environment or environment group.
claims.quote: The policy is applied per environment (or environment group).

claims.claim: Both existing and new agents in scope must follow the configured credential rule.
claims.quote: Once active, all existing and new agents in that environment adhere to this rule, and the types of authentication options for makers change in Copilot Studio.

claims.where: Scope; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Environment group settings override individual environment settings for this policy.
claims.quote: you can't individually disable it for one environment in that group - environment group settings override any environment settings.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The individual environment's credential options are unavailable when it belongs to a group.
claims.quote: If the environment is in a group, the options are unavailable and a message directs you to configure the setting for the group, not the individual environment.

claims.claim: Environment Admin is the documented role for configuring a single environment.
claims.quote: Power Platform admin permissions (Environment Admin for a single environment, or Power Platform Administrator/Global Admin for environment groups).

claims.claim: Power Platform Administrator or Global Admin is required for environment groups.
claims.quote: Power Platform admin permissions (Environment Admin for a single environment, or Power Platform Administrator/Global Admin for environment groups).

claims.claim: Configuring an environment that belongs to a group requires a tenant admin with access to that group.
claims.quote: If the environment you want to configure is part of an environment group, you must be a tenant admin with access to the group.

claims.claim: The update may take a minute to propagate.
claims.quote: The update might take a minute to propagate.

claims.claim: Environment groups can contain only managed environments.
claims.quote: Environment groups can only contain managed environments.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; front matter: licensing.notes; rationale: cost

claims.quote: When you activate managed environments in an environment, all active usage requires one of these standalone licenses or pay-as-you-go meters.

claims.quote: Pay-as-you-go meters for Power Apps per app, Power Pages, and Copilot Studio also qualify.

claims.claim: The licensing model for this specific credential restriction is not yet published.
claims.quote: Searched: "Control maker credential options" "license". Read configure-no-maker-authentication, managed-environment-licensing and billing-licensing excerpts; no control-specific licence was stated.

claims.claim: No meter is documented specifically for this setting at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio "Control maker credential" licensing price meter exception autonomous credentials. Read configure-no-maker-authentication and billing-licensing/requirements-messages-management excerpts; no control-specific meter.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not published a separate price for this control.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio "Control maker credential" licensing price meter exception autonomous credentials. Read configure-no-maker-authentication, managed-environment-licensing and licensing/billing excerpts; no separate control price.

claims.claim: Learn documents no other credential type that remains available under this control when maker credentials are blocked.
claims.quote: Searched: "Control maker credential options" "exception". Read configure-no-maker-authentication and add-tools-custom-agent; neither documents another surviving credential type for this enforcement.

claims.claim: The feature's Learn page does not name MCP tools.
claims.quote: Searched: "Control maker credential options" "MCP". Read configure-no-maker-authentication in full; it names connectors, built-in actions and embedded Power Automate flows, but not MCP.

claims.claim: Learn documents no single-agent exception to the credential restriction for an autonomous agent.
claims.quote: Searched: "Control maker credential options" "exception". Read configure-no-maker-authentication; no single-agent exemption is documented.

claims.claim: The credential control is in Power Platform admin center under Manage > Environments (or Environment groups) > environment > Settings > Product > Features > Copilot Studio agents > Control maker credential options.
claims.quote: select Manage. ... Select Environments or Environment groups. ... select Settings on the top menu bar. Expand the Product section, and select Features. ... Scroll to the Copilot Studio agents section. ... Under Control maker credential options

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls table; Governance controls; Open questions; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: No PowerShell, REST, Power Platform API or pac CLI equivalent is documented for Control maker credential options.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio "Control maker credential options" PowerShell REST API pac CLI. Read configure-no-maker-authentication and pac copilot/copilot-studio excerpts; no equivalent credential-policy call.

claims.claim: The environment sharing control is at Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Features > Sharing agents with embedded maker credentials in Power Platform admin center.
claims.quote: Go to Manage > Environments, and then select the environment that you want to configure. ... Select Settings, and then select Features. ... Find Sharing agents with embedded maker credentials.

claims.claim: An API or automation equivalent for the environment-level embedded-credential sharing control is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Sharing agents with embedded maker credentials" "API" "PowerShell". Read configure-sharing-agents-embedded-maker-credentials and admin-sharing-controls-limits excerpts; no equivalent call.

claims.claim: The complete Threat detection path is Security > Threat detection > Sharing agent with embedded maker credentials > Set up.
claims.quote: In the Environment groups tab, select the environment group for which you want to configure the setting. ... In the Environments tab, select the environment for which you want to configure the setting. ... Select Set up.
claims.fix: Replace the path in controls[2].ui and the rendered table with 'Security > Threat detection > Sharing agent with embedded maker credentials > Environment groups (or Environments) > environment group (or environment) > Set up'. The cited page requires choosing the tab and target before Set up.

claims.claim: An API or automation equivalent for the environment/group sharing control is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Sharing agents with embedded maker credentials" "API" "PowerShell". Read security/control-sharing-agents-with-embedded-maker-credentials and sharing-control excerpts; no equivalent call.

claims.where: controls[3].ui; Governance controls table; Governance controls; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The maker chooses tool credentials under Tools > tool > Details > Additional details > Authentication.
claims.quote: Go to the Tools page for your agent, and select the tool from the list of tools. ... Details ... Additional details ... Authentication: Select whether to use the user's (End user) or maker's (Maker-provided) credentials for the tool.
claims.fix: Keep the cited path, but add that https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/advanced-connectors calls the connector field 'Credentials to use' under Overview > Details > Additional details, whereas the general tools page calls it 'Authentication'. Cite both rather than implying identical labels in every tool experience.

claims.claim: An API or automation equivalent for selecting a tool's end-user versus maker credentials is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio tool Authentication Maker-provided End user configure API YAML connectionReferences. Read add-tools-custom-agent and connection/authentication excerpts; no equivalent call.

claims.claim: Individual tools default to user authentication.
claims.quote: Authentication: Select whether to use the user's (End user) or maker's (Maker-provided) credentials for the tool. By default, user authentication applies.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls table; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: The separate embedded-credential sharing control governs publishing and sharing, not runtime execution.
claims.quote: The sharing agents with embedded maker credentials control governs sharing and publishing. It doesn’t block an agent while the agent is running.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls table; Governance controls
claims.claim: Enabling sharing enforcement does not retroactively unshare existing agents.
claims.quote: Enabling enforcement doesn’t retroactively unshare or disable agents that were previously shared.

claims.claim: The environment sharing control provides All sharing allowed and Safe sharing enforced modes.
claims.quote: To provide detection and guidance without blocking, select All sharing allowed. Or, to block unsafe sharing paths, select Safe sharing enforced.

claims.claim: The Threat detection sharing-control documentation is preview/prerelease and subject to change.
claims.quote:
Control sharing agents with embedded maker credentials (preview)

[This article is prerelease documentation and is subject to change.]

claims.where: controls[2].governs; controls[2].scope; controls[2].note; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The Threat detection sharing control can be configured per environment or environment group.
claims.quote: You can configure the setting for an individual environment or an environment group.

claims.claim: All sharing allowed provides detection and guidance about embedded maker-credential risks without blocking sharing.
claims.quote: Start in a development or validation environment and select All sharing allowed. Use the resulting guidance to understand which agents and flows rely on embedded maker credentials.
